stem: Which population has a much greater incidence of post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis?

options.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples
Children with asymptomatic microscopic haematuria only

explanation: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples have a much greater incidence of post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Nephritic Syndrome and Haematuria

optionExplanations.A: Correct because Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples are specifically noted to have a much greater incidence of post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because urate crystals are a neonatal urine finding and do not describe the higher-incidence population for post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis is a different renal diagnosis and not the population group identified here.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because isolated hypertension in adolescents is not the population specifically associated with a much greater incidence of post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because asymptomatic microscopic haematuria alone does not identify the group with a much greater incidence of post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis.
